nuggets.title: ANN Retrieval Timeout Empties the Candidate Pool

scenario.symptoms: Home feed shows generic trending only for 20% of users during peak. p99 retrieval stage exceeds 120ms budget and ranker receives zero candidates.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Two-stage recommenders treat ANN timeout as empty result without fallback to inverted index or cached candidates.

incident.headline: Hard dependency on slow ANN retrieval yields blank feeds instead of degraded candidates

agenda.goal: Retrieve candidates within budget using sharded ANN, timeouts, and fallback retrieval paths.
agenda.opener: When vector search timed out, users saw only trending. How do you retrieve hundreds of candidates fast enough to rank?

evidence.strong: Sharded ANN with per-shard top-k and timeout, approximate then refine, fallback to co-occurrence or subscription index, cache recent candidates per user.
evidence.adequate: Single ANN index without timeout handling.

misconceptions.pattern: Single global ANN query at billion scale.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens at p99 when one shard is hot?

probes: What candidates do you show if ANN fails?
How many candidates does ranker need?
agenda.referenceFix: ANN with shard timeouts plus inverted-index fallback and cached personal candidates.

nuggets.title: Clickbait Feedback Loop Dominates Ranker Training

scenario.symptoms: Average watch time drops 15% while click-through rises. Model amplifies misleading thumbnails because training labels are click-only.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Daily retrain uses logistic loss on clicks without watch-time or satisfaction labels; creators gamify titles.

incident.headline: Click-only training feedback creates exploitative recommendation feedback loop

agenda.goal: Train on watch-time, satisfaction, and debiased implicit feedback rather than clicks alone.
agenda.opener: CTR went up but viewers watch less. What signals do you learn from and how do you avoid clickbait loops?

evidence.strong: Multi-objective labels with watch time and completion, position debiasing, creator quality penalties, explore/exploit, human eval on holdout.
evidence.adequate: Adds watch time feature without changing primary loss.

misconceptions.challenge: Does a click on a misleading thumbnail help the user?

probes: What stops creators gaming the objective?
agenda.referenceFix: Train on expected watch time with debiasing; guardrails on misleading content features.

nuggets.title: New Creator Videos Never Leave Explore Pool

scenario.symptoms: Uploads from new channels get under 50 impressions unless creator is manually featured. Ranker scores rely on channel historical watch hours unavailable for new accounts.
scenario.interviewerSetup: No exploration bucket or content-based retrieval boost; model defaults cold items to global prior near zero.

incident.headline: Cold-start ranker scores trap new creator content without exploration impressions

agenda.goal: Give new videos impressions via content features, exploration slots, and smoothed priors.
agenda.opener: A new creator's first video never gets recommended. How does it get initial impressions?

evidence.strong: Content embedding similarity, small guaranteed explore traffic, smoothed channel priors, separate cold-start ranker, cap spam uploads.

misconceptions.challenge: How does a brand-new video get its first 100 views?

probes: What content signals exist on upload day?
How much explore traffic is safe?
agenda.referenceFix: Explore bucket plus content-based retrieval boost for fresh uploads.

nuggets.title: Stale User Features Recommend Yesterday's Interests

scenario.symptoms: Users binge a new topic but feed keeps pushing old genre for 6 hours. Real-time clicks not reflected in ranker feature store refresh lag.
scenario.interviewerSetup: User embedding updated batch every 4 hours in offline store; online serving reads cached features without streaming updates.

incident.headline: Batch-only user features lag behind session intent during ranking

agenda.goal: Blend near-line feature updates with batch embeddings for responsive ranking.
agenda.opener: User watched cooking videos all morning but still sees gaming clips. How fresh are ranking features at serve time?

evidence.strong: Lambda architecture: batch base features plus real-time delta from stream, session-level features in ranker, TTL cache invalidation on events.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes daily batch is enough for feed.
misconceptions.challenge: How quickly should a click change the next page?

agenda.referenceFix: Online feature store updates from click stream; ranker combines session + user embedding.

nuggets.title: Offline Lift Does Not Match Online Experiment

scenario.symptoms: New ranker shows +5% offline AUC but online A/B is flat and long-session users churn. Offline eval uses random negatives not matching production candidate generator.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Offline pipeline scores held-out clicks against uniform random videos instead of hard negatives from retrieval stage.

incident.headline: Misaligned offline evaluation overestimates ranker quality versus production candidate distribution

agenda.goal: Evaluate rankers with production-like negatives, interleaving, and online guardrail metrics.
agenda.opener: Offline metrics loved the model but online experiment showed nothing. How do you evaluate recommendation changes?

evidence.strong: Sampled negatives from retrieval, counterfactual eval where possible, interleaving tests, online watch-time and churn guardrails, segment metrics.

misconceptions.challenge: Are random negatives as hard as retrieval candidates?

probes: Where do offline negatives come from?
hints: Match eval to serving candidate set.
agenda.referenceFix: Hard negatives from logged retrieval sets; interleaving before full A/B.
